title: Ops bias / hour-elevation calibration

protocol.name: year2022_2023
protocol.test: the whole 2023 window (report only — never fitted, never selected on)
protocol.model note: the clearness calibration is additive and off by default; the inference code is unchanged

gates.name: GATE: |bias| down on the 2022 validation window
gates.target: smaller than the W2 baseline (4,558 W)
gates.observed: 4,558 W — unchanged: the selection kept the shrinkage at 0.0, so no correction was applied
gates.note: The calibration *can* remove the bias (at shrinkage 1.0 the validation bias moves from +4,776 W to -2,649 W), but it costs 12 % of the MAE, so the bias-first selection rule rejects it.

gates.name: GATE: MAE not materially worse on the 2022 validation window
gates.target: not more than 2 % worse than the W2 baseline

gates.name: The correction is a *level* error, not a tail error
gates.target: diagnostic: the model's median clearness is unbiased
gates.observed: the median log-ratio residual is +0.03 (validation) and -0.004 (training) while the mean is -0.17: the bias lives in the tail, so a level shift trades MAE for bias
gates.note: A bin-wise level correction cannot fix a skewed bias without moving the rows that are already right. The machinery lands and stays off by default; the lever for a tail bias is the ensemble spread, not the level.

gates.name: Nothing fitted on 2023
gates.target: the offsets are fitted on train_2022 and the shrinkage is selected on validate_2022

allowed: The calibration machinery works end to end and is off by default.
The selection rejected every candidate, so the operational model is bit-identical to the W2 baseline.
The model's clearness bias is a tail effect, not a level error.
forbidden: Any claim that W3 improved the model: it did not, and the default is unchanged.
Any claim that the bias was removed.

notes: The first implementation fitted the offsets with a plain mean; 90 rows where the plant delivered nothing (a real outage, not a gap) turned the mean log-ratio into -inf. The estimator is now a trimmed mean over the rows that are actually clearness observations, with a shrinkage prior of 50 rows and a minimum of 20 rows per bin.
The fitting windows are spread across the whole training split; the operational evaluation windows still tile the split from its start, which is the v3 behaviour.
